evidence: Harvard University Archives biography states Irving Babbitt left Montana after two years to pursue postgraduate studies in Pali literature and Buddhist traditions at the Écoles des Hautes-Études in Paris.
source_type: authoritative Harvard archival finding aid, HUG 1185
implication_for_Lovejoy: A Harvard scholar immediately preceding Lovejoy had already followed the exact Harvard/US -> Paris EPHE -> Pali/Buddhist trajectory Lovejoy later reportedly expected.
caution: HOLLIS biography does not itself name Sylvain Lévi as Babbitt's teacher.

evidence: A Presses de l'Inalco scholarly chapter states that Babbitt spent a year at EPHE under Sylvain Lévi studying Pali and Sanskrit.
implication_for_Lovejoy: Supplies the missing teacher edge Babbitt -> Lévi and makes Babbitt a concrete US/Harvard carrier of knowledge about Lévi's Pali teaching.
caution: Until a contemporary enrollment/course record or Babbitt note is recovered, keep the teacher edge as scholarly reconstruction rather than a directly inspected primary component.

evidence: Babbitt returned to the US, earned Harvard A.M. in 1893 in classical literature and ancient Eastern languages, taught at Williams, then returned to Harvard in 1894 as Instructor of French.
implication_for_Lovejoy: Babbitt was resident on Harvard faculty by the time Lovejoy entered Harvard graduate study in 1895.
caution: Institutional co-presence does not establish acquaintance or advice.

evidence: Harvard Crimson elective announcement identifies Irving Babbitt as Instructor in French and says he would conduct French A in the coming year.
implication_for_Lovejoy: Hard contemporary confirmation of Babbitt's active teaching presence during Lovejoy's Harvard period.
caution: No evidence Lovejoy enrolled in French A.

evidence: Lanman's first of three Harvard public lectures on Buddhism explicitly covered relation to Sankhya/Vedanta, northern/southern literature, Sanskrit/Pali, Tipitaka, Pali Text Society, and Siamese edition.
source_type: contemporary Harvard Crimson abstract from Lanman's printed outline
implication_for_Lovejoy: Lovejoy's Harvard environment already publicly taught the exact Sanskrit/Pali/Buddhist/Sankhya distinctions that later frame his 004/JAOS/Paris work.
caution: No evidence yet Lovejoy attended the lecture series; environment/control only.

evidence: Henry Clarke Warren's Buddhism in Translations appeared as Harvard Oriental Series III, edited by Lanman, translated from original Pali, and dedicated to Lanman as Warren's friend and teacher.
implication_for_Lovejoy: Shows an active Harvard Pali-Buddhist translation production network contemporaneous with Lovejoy's training, not just one lecturer's private expertise.
caution: No direct evidence yet Lovejoy read Warren's volume; source-overlap search should be separate.

evidence: HUG 1185 contains Student Materials, 1881-1893; old call HUG 1185.4 'Notes, graduate study'; and old HUG 1185.8 'Manuscript of Dhammapada' moved to Writings/Lectures.
implication_for_Lovejoy: Babbitt's own pre-Harvard-return student papers may preserve the Paris/EPHE/Pali layer and could eventually test exactly what he carried back to Harvard.
caution: HOLLIS reports Digital content = 0 and donor permission required; not an immediate electronic scan target.

evidence: Babbitt and Lovejoy were simultaneously at Harvard during Lovejoy's graduate period, while Babbitt had recently returned from Pali/Buddhist study in Paris under the Lévi network.
status: network topology secure; interpersonal edge unproved
implication_for_Lovejoy: For the first time there is a concrete resident Harvard person who could in principle have transmitted a recommendation/reputation of Lévi's Pali teaching to Lovejoy.
caution: Do not say Babbitt advised Lovejoy, that they met, or that Lovejoy learned of Lévi from him without correspondence/course/advising evidence.

evidence: Babbitt's posthumous Dhammapada translation was explicitly translated from Pali; Harvard archive preserves its manuscript predecessor.
implication_for_Lovejoy: Confirms Babbitt's Paris Pali interest was durable rather than a biographical footnote.
caution: Later publication does not show what Babbitt said to Lovejoy in the 1890s.
